parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain how enzymes lower the activation energy needed to allow reactions to proceed.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
Folic acid is a molecule used by all cells for growth. Bacteria cannot absorb folic acid from their surroundings. Bacteria use an enzyme to make a molecule called PABA. PABA is used to make folic acid.

An investigation was carried out to determine the effect on the production of PABA when the concentration of an enzyme inhibitor is increased. Four different concentrations ($1 \mu\text{M}$ to $30 \mu\text{M}$) of the inhibitor were used, together with a control with no inhibitor.

The concentration of PABA produced in each reaction mixture was determined at 10 minute intervals.

The results are shown in Fig. 2.1.

{{figure:figure_2_1.webp}}
parts.text: Use Fig. 2.1 to describe the results of the investigation.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Outline an experiment that could be carried out to determine whether the inhibitor of the enzyme that catalyses the reaction to produce PABA is competitive or non-competitive.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.stem: Folic acid from the diet is able to enter human cells, but is **not** able to cross bacterial cell walls. Human cells do **not** have an enzyme to make PABA.
parts.text: Suggest why the inhibitor of this enzyme could be used as a drug to treat bacterial infections in humans.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Suggest why there are few drugs that have any effect on viruses.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: The search for new antibiotics is important because there are many strains of bacteria that are resistant to antibiotics.
parts.text: Suggest two ways to reduce the spread of antibiotic resistance.
